standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness of the functors attached to a point
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the fact that the pullback and pushforward of a morphism of topoi are left exact
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the final object is preserved, which is the base case of the argument.

core_obligations: The adjunction map (proof lines 8399-8402): there is always a map from the stalk of the pushforward to the set, and it is an isomorphism on the final object because the two functors are left exact.

The map from the set to the stalk (proof lines 8402-8410): for an element of the set the author transports the isomorphism on the final object along the corresponding map from a point, producing the required map; the two displayed maps are canonically defined and their composite is the identity.
proof_roadmap: Recall the adjunction map and check it is an isomorphism for the final object.
Transport that isomorphism along the maps determined by elements of the set.
Obtain the second canonical map and conclude that the composite is the identity.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces canonical maps between a set and the stalk of its pushforward along a point of a topos, whose composite is the identity (statement lines 8386-8396). The proof is a short but complete argument: the adjunction supplies the map from the stalk to the set and it is an isomorphism on the final object because both functors are left exact (proof lines 8399-8402); the author then transports this isomorphism along the maps determined by the elements of the set to obtain the map in the other direction (proof lines 8402-8410), and the composite is the identity by construction. The non-formal content is the transport along the elements. The claim is H1: a short construction with the exactness input named.
